newsitem.title: UK: Lasmo reports Pakistan gas field discovery.
newsitem.headline: Lasmo reports Pakistan gas field discovery.

text.p: Lasmo Plc on Tuesday reported the discovery of a new gas field after successful drilling of an exploration well in the Kirthar Concession in Western Sindh, Pakistan.

"The well has confirmed the presence of an excellent hydrocarbon province and has increased the attractiveness of several other prospects and leads within this concession...," said Lasmo's chief operating officer John Hogan.
Lasmo has a 47.5 percent interest in the Kirthar Concession.
Shell Exploration Pakistan BV also has a 47.5 percent working interest, while Pakistan's state-owned Oil and Gas Development Corporation has 5.0 percent.

Lasmo said an appraisal of the new discovery and evaluation of the wider Kirthar area will start later this year. This will entail a comprehensive seismic survey, folowed by a sustained drilling programme.
Lasmo shares rose six pence to 229 pence in pre-market trading after they had already been squeezed higher late in March amid speculation of a discovery in Pakistan.
Pakistan is one of Lasmo's core areas next to Britain, Indonesia, North Africa and Italy.
The Bhit-2 well in Pakistan was drilled to test a large surface anticlinal feature to a total depth of 2,067 metres.
The entire section of the objective Cretaceous Pab Sandstone was found to be gas bearing and 150 metres of net gas pay were encountered.
Further hydrocarbon indications were seen below the sandstone to the total depth of the well.
"The success of this well has confirmed the substantial reserves potential of Bhit," Lasmo said.
